1.1: This Paul talkin'—an apostle, but not one made by people or some group of men. Naw, I was sent by Jesus Christ Himself, and God the Father, the one who raised Jesus from the dead.
1.2: And all the brothers with me? They co-signin' this too. To the churches out in Galatia—
1.3: Grace and peace to y'all from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ,
1.4: the One who gave His whole self up for our sins, so He could snatch us out this evil world we livin' in—just like God the Father wanted.
1.5: All glory belong to Him, now and forever. Amen.
1.6: I'm honestly shocked—y'all switched up so fast. Turnin' away from the One who called y'all through the grace of Christ, and runnin' to a whole other gospel?
1.7: Not that it's even another real one—these folks just tryna stir stuff up and twist up the real gospel of Christ.
1.8: Listen, I don't care if it's me, or even some angel floatin' down from heaven—if they preach somethin' different than what we already told y'all? Let them be cursed.
1.9: Matter fact, let me say it again—if anybody preaches somethin' other than what you already heard from us? Let them be cursed, period.
1.10: Who you think I'm tryin' to please—God or people? If I was still out here tryna be a people-pleaser, I couldn't call myself a servant of Christ.
1.11: Let me make this crystal clear, fam: the gospel I preached? It ain't man-made.
1.12: I ain't get this from nobody teachin' me. I didn't go to school for it. I got it straight from Jesus, revealed to me personally.
1.13: Y'all already heard how I used to live—deep in Judaism. I was wildin'. I used to persecute God's church bad—tryna shut it all the way down.
1.14: And I was movin' up fast in the Jewish scene, way ahead of my age group. I was mad committed to all the traditions passed down to me.
1.15: But when God—yeah, the same one who had me set apart from birth—decided to call me through His grace…
1.16: …and let His Son be revealed in me (so I could preach to the Gentiles), I ain't go run and ask nobody for advice.
1.17: I didn't hit up the apostles in Jerusalem right away either. I went out to Arabia first. Then I came back to Damascus.
1.18: Three years later, I finally went to Jerusalem to link up with Peter. I stayed with him for about 15 days.
1.19: I ain't see none of the other apostles—just James, Jesus' brother.
1.20: And just so y'all know—I ain't lyin'. God sees me. I'm tellin' the truth.
1.21: After that, I bounced to Syria and Cilicia.
1.22: The churches in Judea didn't even know me by face yet.
1.23: They just kept hearin' stories like: "Yo, that same dude who used to come for us is now out here preachin' the same faith he tried to shut down."
1.24: And because of that? They gave God all the glory.

2.1: Fourteen years later, I went back up to Jerusalem. I brought Barnabas with me—and I brought Titus too.
2.2: I ain't just go on my own. I went 'cause God told me to. I shared the gospel I been preachin' to the Gentiles—especially with the leaders, behind closed doors, just in case everything I'd done would've ended up pointless.
2.3: But guess what? Even Titus, who's a full-on Greek, wasn't forced to get circumcised.
2.4: This whole issue came up 'cause of some fake brothers who snuck in on purpose to spy on our freedom in Christ. They tryna drag us back into bondage.
2.5: But we ain't fold—not for a second. We didn't give in, so that the truth of the gospel could stay pure for y'all.
2.6: Now, as for those folks who thought they was important—it don't mean nothin' to me. God don't play favorites. They didn't add anything new to what I was preachin'.
2.7: On the flip side, they realized I had been called to preach to the uncircumcised (the Gentiles)—just like Peter was sent to the circumcised (the Jews).
2.8: 'Cause the same God who gave Peter the juice to reach the Jews, gave me that same power to reach the Gentiles.
2.9: And when James, Peter (Cephas), and John—the so-called "pillars"—saw the grace God put on me, they gave me and Barnabas the handshake. Like, "Aight, y'all got the Gentiles, we got the Jews."
2.10: The only thing they asked was that we remember the poor—and I was already on that anyway.
2.11: Now let me tell y'all what went down in Antioch—Peter came through and I had to call him out, face to face, 'cause he was straight-up wrong.
2.12: Before some folks from James showed up, he was cool eatin' with the Gentiles. But when they came? He switched up, pulled back, 'cause he was scared of what the religious folks would say.
2.13: And that same two-faced behavior spread—even the rest of the Jews started actin' funny, and yep… even Barnabas got caught up in it.
2.14: I couldn't sit quiet. I told Peter in front of everybody: "Bruh, you Jewish—but you livin' like a Gentile right now. So why you tryna force Gentiles to live like Jews?"
2.15: We're Jews by birth, not 'Gentile sinners.'
2.16: But even we know this: nobody gets right with God by following the law. We believed in Jesus so we could be made right through faith, not through rule-keeping. 'Cause if law could save us, we'd all be doomed. Ain't nobody justified by law.
2.17: Now if we put our faith in Christ, but we still mess up—does that make Jesus the cause of our sin? No way.
2.18: If I go back to rebuild what I already tore down, that just proves I'm wrong—not Jesus.
2.19: Look, I died to that law life so I could live for God.
2.20: I ain't even the one livin' anymore—Christ is livin' through me now. The life I got now in this body? I live it by faith in Jesus—the One who loved me and gave Himself up for me. That's personal.
2.21: I ain't tossin' God's grace aside. 'Cause if bein' made right with God could come from the law, then Jesus died for nothin'.

3.1: Yo, Galatians, what's wrong with y'all? Who bewitched you to turn away from the truth? You saw Christ crucified in front of you—now you actin' like you don't know what's good?
3.2: Hold up. Let me ask you this: Did you get the Holy Spirit by followin' the law, or by hearing the gospel and believing?
3.3: Are y'all really that foolish? You started out in the Spirit—now you think you gon' finish it off by your own effort? Like that's how growth works?
3.4: You've been through so much already—and you really gon' let that go to waste? You think it was all in vain?
3.5: So the God who gave y'all the Spirit and did miracles among you—was He doin' that 'cause y'all followed the law, or because you believed the gospel?
3.6: Just like Abraham, who believed God—and that faith was counted as righteousness.
3.7: Understand this: the true sons of Abraham ain't just his bloodline, but those who live by faith.
3.8: Scripture told us God would justify the Gentiles by faith way back in Abraham's time. When God said, "In you, all nations will be blessed," He wasn't just talkin' to Jews.
3.9: So those who live by faith are blessed with faithful Abraham.
3.10: But for those who depend on the law? They're under the curse. Why? 'Cause the law says: "Cursed is everyone who doesn't do everything the law says."
3.11: Ain't no way to be justified by the law in God's eyes. It's clear: "The righteous shall live by faith."
3.12: But the law ain't about faith—it's about doing. The law says, "Live by it, or else."
3.13: Christ redeemed us from that curse. He became a curse for us. He took the hit, like the law said: "Cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree." Jesus switched up the game—He got on that cross, so we could get the blessing of Abraham.
3.14: All this happened so the Gentiles could get in on the blessing and receive the Holy Spirit through faith.
3.15: Let me break it down like this: Even if it's just a regular contract, once it's confirmed, nobody can change it. God's promises? Ain't like contracts with people—they're eternal and can't be tampered with.
3.16: Now God made promises to Abraham and his Seed. It wasn't about "seeds" (many) but about one Seed—Jesus. Jesus is the promise that holds everything together.
3.17: Here's the thing: the law came 430 years later, but it don't change the promise God gave before. If the inheritance was based on the law, then it wouldn't be a promise anymore. God gave it to Abraham as a promise.
3.18: If the inheritance comes from followin' the law, then it ain't a promise no more. But God gave it to Abraham as a promise, not by works.
3.19: So what's the purpose of the law then? It came because of sin—to show us we needed a Savior, until the promised Seed (Jesus) came. It was put in place by angels, and Moses was the mediator.
3.20: But a mediator only works for more than one person—God is one.
3.21: Does this mean the law goes against God's promises? Nope. If there was a law that could give life, we'd have been justified by it. The law shows us we all fall short—so we can't do it on our own. We need Jesus.
3.22: The law confined us all under sin, so the promise could be given to those who believe in Jesus.
3.23: Before faith came, we were kept under the law, locked up, waiting for the faith that was about to be revealed.
3.24: The law was our tutor—pointin' us straight to Christ. It taught us that we can't save ourselves. It was a set-up for faith.
3.25: But now that faith has come? We ain't under the tutor no more. We live by faith.
3.26: Y'all are God's sons through faith in Christ Jesus.
3.27: And since all of y'all who've been baptized into Christ have put Him on—y'all wear Him like a new identity.
3.28: There's no more Jew, no more Greek, no more slave, no more free, no more male or female. In Christ—we're all one.
3.29: And if you belong to Christ? Then you are Abraham's seed—heirs to the promise.

4.1: Aight, let me break this down: an heir might be master of everything, but as long as he's a child, he's basically treated the same as a slave. He still gotta listen to the guardians and caretakers 'til it's time for him to take over.
4.2: Same for us—when we were kids, we were stuck under the world's rules, no freedom.
4.3: But when the time was right, God sent His Son, born of a woman, born under the law,
4.4: to redeem us, those trapped under the law, and give us the adoption as sons.
4.5: And now that we're His sons? God sent the Spirit of His Son into our hearts, and now we call out to Him—"Abba, Father!"
4.6: So you ain't a slave no more. You a son. And if you a son, you an heir of God through Christ.
4.7: So, you ain't a slave no more, you a son—and if you a son, you an heir of God through Christ.
4.8: But hold up—back when y'all didn't know God, you were servin' all these false gods, things that ain't even real.
4.9: Now you know God, or better yet, God knows you, so how come y'all wanna go back to that old stuff?
4.10: Y'all wanna be enslaved again to things like days, months, seasons, and years.
4.11: I'm worried for you—did I labor for y'all for nothing?
4.12: Yo, become like me, I became like y'all. We're in this together—you haven't wronged me at all.
4.13: Y'all remember when I came to you—sick—and still preached the gospel to you?
4.14: And my condition? Y'all didn't turn away from me. You treated me like I was Christ Himself.
4.15: What happened to all that love? Y'all even said you'd pluck out your eyes for me if you could.
4.16: So now, I'm your enemy just 'cause I'm speakin' the truth to you?
4.17: These false teachers? They zealously court you—but for the wrong reasons. They tryna cut you off from me, so you can be loyal to them instead.
4.18: But it's good to be zealous for good stuff—not just when I'm around, but always.
4.19: I'm like a momma in labor, tryna give birth to Christ in you. I'm not even sure where y'all stand with this, but I'm still working on it.
4.20: I wish I could be with y'all right now and change my tone, 'cause I'm confused about where y'all at spiritually.
4.21: Aight, let me ask y'all: You who want to go back under the law—do you even understand what the law is about?
4.22: It's written: Abraham had two sons: one by the slave woman, and one by the free woman.
4.23: The one born of the slave woman was born by human effort; the one born of the free woman came by promise.
4.24: This story's a symbol—it's about the two covenants:
4.25: Hagar is Mount Sinai in Arabia—and that corresponds to Jerusalem now, where people are still in bondage.
4.26: But the Jerusalem above—that's free. That's the true mother of us all.
4.27: Just like the Scripture says: "Rejoice, barren woman! Shout out loud, you who've never had kids! The one who was deserted is about to have more children than the one with a husband!"
4.28: We, the ones of promise, just like Isaac—we're not just children of the law, we're children of the promise.
4.29: And just like it was back then, the one born of the flesh (Ishmael) persecuted the one born of the Spirit (Isaac)—that's still happening today.
4.30: But listen to what Scripture says: "Cast out the slave woman and her son, 'cause the son of the slave woman won't inherit with the son of the free woman."
4.31: So, family, we ain't children of the slave woman—we children of the free.

5.1: Aight, listen—stand strong in the freedom Christ gave us. Don't let yourself get caught back up in that old law, that yoke of bondage.
5.2: I'm tellin' y'all straight: if you get circumcised, Christ ain't gonna profit you.
5.3: You still gotta follow every single law, not just one. You can't pick and choose.
5.4: So, if you're tryna be justified by the law, you're cut off from Christ. You've fallen from grace.
5.5: But we, through the Spirit, are waiting for that righteousness by faith.
5.6: Look, in Christ, whether you're circumcised or not, it don't matter. It's all about faith that works through love.
5.7: Y'all were runnin' strong, but who tripped you up from obeying the truth?
5.8: That kind of thinking ain't from God, the One who called you.
5.9: Just like yeast spreads through dough, a little bad doctrine messes up everything.
5.10: But I'm confident in you, that you won't let these distractions mess you up. And whoever keeps trippin' you up? They gon' face judgment.
5.11: If I'm still preachin' circumcision, why am I still being persecuted? If I was about that life, the offense of the cross would've disappeared.
5.12: Honestly, I wish the people messin' with y'all would just cut themselves off.
5.13: You've been called to freedom—don't use that freedom to do whatever your flesh wants. Nah, use that freedom to serve each other in love.
5.14: All the laws, all the rules—they come down to this one thing: "Love your neighbor as yourself."
5.15: But if y'all out here biting and devouring each other, you'll destroy yourselves.
5.16: Here's what I'm sayin'—walk by the Spirit, and you won't give in to the lust of the flesh.
5.17: The flesh and the Spirit warring against each other. They oppose each other. That's why you don't do what you wanna do sometimes.
5.18: But if you're led by the Spirit, you ain't under the law anymore.
5.19: Now, let's talk about the works of the flesh—these are obvious: adultery, fornication, uncleanness, lewdness, idolatry, sorcery, hatred, jealousy, outbursts of wrath, selfish ambition, dissensions, heresies, envy, murders, drunkenness, revelries, and more.
5.20: But here's the fruit of the Spirit—love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control. Against these? No law. This is what God wants.
5.21: Envy, murders, drunkenness, revelries, and all that other mess. I already warned you about this, like I did before—if you out here living like this, you won't inherit the kingdom of God.
5.22: But the fruit of the Spirit is: love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness.
5.23: Gentleness and self-control. Ain't no law against these things.
5.24: Those who belong to Christ have already crucified the flesh—all the desires and passions that come with it.
5.25: If we live by the Spirit, we need to walk in the Spirit.
5.26: Let's not be arrogant or provoke each other. No envy.

6.1: Ayo, if somebody's caught up in sin, y'all who are spiritually mature, help restore them—but do it with gentleness, watchin' yourself so you don't fall into the same temptation.
6.2: Bear each other's burdens—this is how we fulfill Christ's law: love each other and carry each other's weight.
6.3: If you think you're all that but ain't even really all that, you foolin' yourself.
6.4: Take a moment to examine yourself—then you can be proud of your own work, and not compare yourself to someone else.
6.5: Everybody got their own load to carry—don't be worried about somebody else's weight when you got your own to carry.
6.6: If you're learning from the Word, share the good stuff you got with the person teachin' you.
6.7: Don't be fooled—God ain't a joke. Whatever you put out there, you gon' get back.
6.8: If you out here sowin' into your flesh (your selfish desires), you gon' reap corruption. But if you sow into the Spirit, you gon' get eternal life from the Spirit.
6.9: Don't give up doin' good. In the right season, you gon' reap if you don't quit.
6.10: So as long as you have the chance, do good to everyone—especially to those in the family of faith.
6.11: Look at the big letters I'm writin' to y'all with my own hand. I'm serious about this.
6.12: The ones who wanna look good in front of people—they'll try to make you get circumcised. Why? 'Cause they don't wanna get persecuted for Christ's cross.
6.13: They ain't even keeping the law themselves, but they want y'all to get circumcised just so they can brag about it. That's whack.
6.14: But God forbid that I should boast in anything except the cross of Jesus Christ, by which the world is dead to me, and I'm dead to the world.
6.15: Circumcision or uncircumcision? Don't matter. What matters is being a new creation in Christ.
6.16: So, everybody who lives by this rule—peace and mercy be upon them, and on the Israel of God.
6.17: From now on, don't bother me. I carry the marks of Jesus on my body, so I ain't got time for foolishness.
6.18: May the grace of Jesus be with y'all. Amen.
